```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
# rxode2 warns that the occasion-indicator IOV etas are not mu-referenced;
# that affects estimation only, not simulation.
mod <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2019_cyclosporine"))))
cat("* Citation: ", mod$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description: ", mod$description, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2019.00518>\n")
```

Liu 2019 asked whether a single oral dose of baicalin, a flavone glucuronide
used in traditional Chinese medicine whose aglycone baicalein inhibits CYP3A
and P-glycoprotein in vitro, changes the pharmacokinetics of cyclosporine A.
The study analysed whole-blood cyclosporine A by non-compartmental analysis
(the bioequivalence comparison) and by a NONMEM population PK model, which is
the model shipped here. The final model is a two-compartment model with linear
elimination and Savic transit-compartment absorption. Baicalin was tested as a
factor on every structural parameter and had no clinically relevant effect, so
the final model carries no baicalin term.

# Population

Sixteen healthy Chinese volunteers (8 men, 8 women), aged 19-34 years with a
body mass index of 19.4-25.6 kg/m^2 (Methods, "Study Population"), took part in
a single-centre, open-label, two-period, fixed-sequence study. After an
overnight fast each received 200 mg cyclosporine A orally as eight 25 mg
Sandimmun Neoral microemulsion capsules: alone in period 1, and with 500 mg
oral baicalin in period 2 after a 2-week washout. Whole blood was sampled
pre-dose and at 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 24, 36 and 48 h
after each dose; the UHPLC-MS/MS assay had an LLOQ of 10 ng/mL. Body weight is
not reported. The same information is available from
`readModelDb("Liu_2019_cyclosporine")()$population`.

# Source trace

Table 3 prints the median and 95% CI of 1000 bootstrap runs of the final model;
it prints no separate point estimate, so the bootstrap medians are encoded.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Two-compartment disposition, linear elimination, proportional error | -- | Results, "Model Development" |
| Savic transit absorption into an absorption compartment emptied at ka | -- | Methods, "Absorption Model Selection"; Table 2 model M8 |
| `lcl` (CL/F) | 62.8 L/h | Table 3 |
| `lvc` (Vc/F) | 254 L | Table 3 |
| `lvp` (Vp/F) | 388 L | Table 3 |
| `lq` (Q/F) | 23.6 L/h | Table 3 |
| `lka` (Ka) | 12.4 1/h | Table 3 |
| `lmtt` (MTT) | 0.812 h | Table 3 |
| `lntr` (N) | 20.2 | Table 3 |
| `etalcl` | 12.6% CV | Table 3, IIV CL |
| `etalka` | 155% CV | Table 3, IIV Ka |
| `etalq` | 25.7% CV | Table 3, IIV Q |
| `etalntr` | 20.2% CV | Table 3, IIV N |
| `etaiov_mtt_1`, `etaiov_mtt_2` | 4.39% CV | Table 3, IOV MTT |
| `etaiov_ntr_1`, `etaiov_ntr_2` | 17.6% CV | Table 3, IOV N |
| CV% to variance, `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` | -- | Table 3 footnote |
| `propSd` | 19.4% CV, `sqrt(log(1 + 0.194^2))` | Table 3, PRV and footnote |
| Baicalin factor `PAR = TVPAR * theta_test^test`, not retained | -- | Methods Eq. 1; Results; Figure 4 |

# Typical-value profile

The typical-value solve below (all random effects zero) is the check against
which the printed parameters are tested. Mass balance must hold exactly:
`CL/F * AUC(0-inf)` equals the dose. If the analytical transit input silently
returned zero, this check would fail.

```{r typical}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
dense <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48, by = 0.01), seq(48, 600, by = 0.5))))
ev_typ <- data.frame(
  id = 1, time = c(0, dense), evid = c(1, rep(0, length(dense))),
  amt = c(200, rep(0, length(dense))), cmt = c(rep("depot", 1), rep("central", length(dense))),
  OCC = 1
)
typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_typ))
auc_typ <- sum(diff(typ$time) * (head(typ$Cc, -1) + tail(typ$Cc, -1)) / 2) # ng*h/mL
mass_balance <- exp(mod$theta[["lcl"]]) * auc_typ / 1000 / 200
mass_balance
# Exact identity between two sides that use the same parameters; only the
# trapezoid error on a 0.01 h grid and the truncation at 600 h remain.
stopifnot(abs(mass_balance - 1) < 2e-3)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Population predictions (Figure 2B)

Figure 2B plots the observations against the population predictions (PRED) of
the final model. Because every subject received the same dose at the same
nominal times, the PRED values form vertical columns, one per sampling time.
The maintainers read the column positions from the figure by pixel analysis
(axis ticks 200/400/600 ng/mL at 83.5 px per 200 ng/mL). The 6 h column is
wider than the others and is not used.

```{r figure-2b}
fig2b <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~pred_fig2b,
  1.0,   398.8,
  1.5,   474.3,
  2.0,   398.8,
  2.5,   338.9,
  3.0,   288.6,
  4.0,   209.6,
  8.0,   68.3
)
cmp_pred <- fig2b |>
  left_join(typ |> mutate(time = round(time, 2)) |> select(time, Cc), by = "time") |>
  mutate(ratio = Cc / pred_fig2b)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_pred |>
    rename(
      "Time (h)" = time,
      "Figure 2B PRED (ng/mL)" = pred_fig2b,
      "Table 3 typical value (ng/mL)" = Cc,
      "Ratio" = ratio
    ),
  digits = c(1, 1, 1, 3),
  caption = "Typical-value concentrations from the Table 3 parameters vs the PRED columns of Figure 2B."
)
```

The printed Table 3 parameters reproduce the shape of the paper's own
population prediction at every sampling time, but every concentration is about
1.35 times higher. A constant ratio across the absorption peak and the
distribution phase means that only the scale differs: the ratios between the
clearances, the volumes and the absorption constants are right. The same factor
appears in the non-compartmental results below. The 200 mg dose divided by
the typical CL/F of 62.8 L/h gives an AUC(0-inf) of 3.18 ug.h/mL, against a
geometric mean of 2.33 ug.h/mL (CL/F 85.7 L/h) in Table 1, a ratio of 1.36.
No unit, molar-mass or dose reading accounts for this factor, so the model
ships with the parameters as printed. See "Assumptions and deviations" below.

```{r figure-2b-gate}
# Deterministic typical-value solve vs digitised points. A mis-transcribed
# absorption parameter would change the ratio between time points; a
# mis-transcribed CL or V would move the level away from the documented 1.35.
stopifnot(
  sd(cmp_pred$ratio) / mean(cmp_pred$ratio) < 0.03,
  abs(median(cmp_pred$ratio) - 1.355) < 0.04
)
```

# Virtual cohort

There are 200 virtual subjects. Each receives 200 mg at time 0 (period 1,
cyclosporine alone, `OCC = 1`) and again 336 h later (period 2, with baicalin,
`OCC = 2`), matching the 2-week washout. Observations fall at the study's
nominal sampling times plus a denser grid for plotting. The final model has no
covariates and no baicalin term, so the two periods differ only by the
inter-occasion draws on MTT and N.

```{r cohort}
n_sub <- 200
t_period2 <- 336
nominal <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(nominal, seq(0, 6, by = 0.25), seq(6, 48, by = 1))))

doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), period = 1:2) |>
  mutate(time = (period - 1) * t_period2, evid = 1, amt = 200, cmt = "depot")
obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), period = 1:2, tad_nom = obs_times) |>
  mutate(time = (period - 1) * t_period2 + tad_nom, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central") |>
  select(-tad_nom)
events <- bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  mutate(
    OCC = period,
    treatment = ifelse(period == 1, "CsA alone", "CsA + baicalin")
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, period, treatment, OCC)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("treatment", "period")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(tad_h = round(time - (period - 1) * t_period2, 4))
# A silently zero transit input would leave every concentration at 0.
stopifnot(median(sim$Cc[sim$tad_h == 1.5]) > 300)
```

## Visual predictive check (Figure 3)

```{r figure-3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Liu 2019: simulated 2.5th, 50th and 97.5th percentiles of whole-blood cyclosporine A (both periods pooled, residual error included)."}
sim |>
  group_by(tad_h) |>
  summarise(
    Q025 = quantile(sim, 0.025), Q50 = quantile(sim, 0.5), Q975 = quantile(sim, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad_h, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Blood cyclosporine concentration (ng/mL)")
```

# PKNCA validation

The NCA uses the study's nominal sampling times and the simulated observations
with residual error (`sim`). Values below the 10 ng/mL LLOQ are excluded, as in
the study. The treatment grouping is the study period.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(tad_h %in% nominal) |>
  mutate(Cc = dplyr::case_when(
    tad_h == 0 ~ 0,
    sim < 10 ~ NA_real_,
    TRUE ~ sim
  )) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, treatment, time = tad_h, Cc)
stopifnot(all(tapply(sim_nca$time == 0, paste(sim_nca$id, sim_nca$treatment), any)))

dose_nca <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(time = 0) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 48,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Table 1 reports geometric means for AUC, Cmax and t1/2 and the median for Tmax,
so the simulated results are summarised the same way. AUC is reported in
ng.h/mL here (Table 1 prints ug.h/mL).

```{r nca-compare}
geomean <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x[is.finite(x) & x > 0])))
sim_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(
    PPORRES = if (PPTESTCD[1] == "tmax") median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE) else geomean(PPORRES),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,       ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "CsA alone",      541,   1.5,   2190,     2330,        7.44,
  "CsA + baicalin", 558,   1.5,   2220,     2380,        7.60
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_summary,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "h*ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "h*ng/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published NCA (Liu 2019 Table 1, geometric means; Tmax median). * differs from the published value by more than 20%.")
```

The simulated AUCs are 33-36% above Table 1 in both periods. This is the same
scale factor seen against the Figure 2B population predictions, and it follows
directly from the printed CL/F (AUC(0-inf) = 200 mg / 62.8 L/h =
3.18 ug.h/mL). Cmax is 19-26% above Table 1, in line with the typical-value
peak of 639 ng/mL, which is 18% above the observed geometric mean of 541 ng/mL.
Tmax matches.
The simulated NCA half-life (8.9-9.2 h, from the same 48 h window and LLOQ) is
about 20% longer than Table 1's 7.4-7.6 h. The printed micro-constants put the
terminal disposition half-life at about 16.6 h, so in both cases the 48 h NCA
half-life mixes the distribution and terminal phases. The two periods agree
with each other, as in the study, because the final model has no baicalin
effect.

```{r nca-gate}
pct <- sim_summary |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment)) |>
  inner_join(
    published |> pivot_longer(-treatment, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("treatment", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(ratio = PPORRES / ref)
auc_ratio <- pct$ratio[pct$PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "aucinf.obs")]
# Structural: the documented ~1.36 scale factor of the printed CL/F. A wrong
# clearance, dose or unit conversion moves this centre by tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(auc_ratio) - 1.36) < 0.12,
  # Both periods share every structural parameter, so their AUCs must agree.
  abs(diff(pct$PPORRES[pct$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"])) /
    mean(pct$PPORRES[pct$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"]) < 0.1
)
```

# Effect of baicalin (Figure 4)

Baicalin co-administration was tested as a multiplicative factor
(`PAR = TVPAR * theta_test^test`, Methods Eq. 1) on each structural parameter
in turn, each with a 1000-sample bootstrap. The maintainers digitised the
bootstrap medians and 95% CIs from Figure 4. Every CI includes 1, and only Ka
and Q extend beyond the 0.80-1.25 range, which the authors attribute to
pronounced between-subject variability rather than to an interaction. None of
these factors is part of the final model; they are recorded under
`covariatesDataExcluded$CONMED_BAICALIN` in the model file.

```{r figure-4}
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Parameter, ~Median, ~Lower, ~Upper,
  "CL/F",     0.99,    0.95,   1.04,
  "Ka",       0.98,    0.29,   1.49,
  "N",        1.02,    0.89,   1.17,
  "MTT",      1.02,    0.98,   1.05,
  "Vc/F",     0.97,    0.90,   1.03,
  "Vp/F",     1.07,    0.98,   1.15,
  "Q/F",      1.07,    0.95,   1.26
)
knitr::kable(
  fig4 |> rename("Bootstrap median" = Median, "2.5th percentile" = Lower, "97.5th percentile" = Upper),
  caption = "Baicalin effect factors, digitised from Figure 4 of Liu 2019 (not in the final model)."
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **The printed parameters give exposures about 1.35 times the paper's own.**
  The Table 3 typical-value profile is 1.35 times the Figure 2B population
  predictions at every sampling time (CV of the ratio below 3%). The printed
  CL/F of 62.8 L/h gives an AUC(0-inf) 1.36 times the Table 1 geometric mean,
  whose CL/F is 85.7 L/h. The paper's Figure 2B, Figure 3 VPC and Table 1 all
  agree with the observed data, so the defect lies in the printed scale of the
  clearances and volumes (CL/F, Vc/F, Vp/F and Q/F would all need to be about
  1.35 times larger), not in the model structure. No unit, molar-mass,
  blood-to-plasma or dose reading explains the factor; for example a 150 mg
  dose would give 1.33, outside the precision of the Figure 2B reading.
  Rescaling the parameters to match would tune the model to a validation
  target, so the parameters ship exactly as printed. No erratum was found
  (literature check, 2026-11-25). Users who need the observed exposure level
  of this study should be aware of this.
- **Bootstrap medians, not final estimates.** Table 3 prints only the bootstrap
  median and 95% CI of each parameter, so the medians are encoded.
- **Transit-compartment form.** The paper names the transit compartment model
  but prints no equation. The Savic 2007 form with a non-integer N
  (`ktr = (N + 1) / MTT`) and a separate absorption rate constant Ka into the
  central compartment is assumed, since N is estimated as a continuous value
  (20.2) with between-subject and between-occasion variability.
- **Variability scales.** IIV and IOV are encoded as log-normal with
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`, following the CV% formula in the Table 3
  footnote. The proportional residual SD is `sqrt(log(1 + 0.194^2)) = 0.1922`
  from the same footnote; the plain `CV = sigma` reading (0.194) differs by
  less than 1%.
- **Occasions.** One occasion per study period (`OCC = 1` cyclosporine alone,
  `OCC = 2` with baicalin), with the occasion-2 IOV variances fixed equal to
  occasion 1. The paper does not state the occasion definition; the
  two-period design makes this the only natural reading.
- **No baicalin effect, no covariates.** None of the tested covariates (age,
  weight, sex, hematocrit, ALT, AST, total bilirubin, albumin) and no baicalin
  factor was retained, so the model has no covariate terms. They are documented
  under `covariatesDataExcluded`.
